steps: Warm up and review technique, especially swings and overhead movements; warm-up is additional to the listed duration. Choose a manageable load, clear the space and use a stable surface.
Set a ten-minute timer. One round: ten swings, eight goblet squats, six push presses (three per arm) and four burpees with crossings. Repeat in order and rest as needed.
Stop at the signal. Score completed rounds plus repetitions in the unfinished round; each round has twenty-eight reps. The crossing after a burpee is not a separate rep.

Kettlebell swing: grip with both hands, hinge hips back with slightly bent knees, then extend hips so the bell floats no higher than shoulder level. Avoid lifting with the shoulders or arching your back.
Goblet squat: hold the bell with both hands close to your chest, lower hips with feet stable and knees tracking toes, then stand with control.
Push press: from a one-arm rack, dip the knees slightly, then extend the legs and press the bell overhead. Return to the shoulder with control; do three per arm.

Burpee over the bell: place a stable bell on the floor with ample clearance and keep hands off it. Perform a burpee beside it, then cross to the other side with control. The brief includes a jump over the bell; the safer editorial option is to go around it without jumping an obstacle. Each burpee plus crossing counts as one repetition.

Keep breathing and set the bell down with control before switching sides. Rest when technique deteriorates and stop for pain or dizziness. Extra breaks extend an interval session; in EMOM or AMRAP reduce work within the same timer.
en.recommendationReason: For an experienced exerciser seeking a timed circuit. Score completed rounds plus extra repetitions; record going around rather than jumping and any other modifications.
